answer: Sybil resistance starts at a single admission jetty: a new agent may enter only after locking slashable stake and being added as a vertex in a work-attestation graph. Edges form when established peers countersign real tasks, so a cheap clone cluster collapses to one bonded vertex. That vertex also carries a unique pigment—the hashed trail of its attested output—which peers check at the jetty before granting voting weight or reward share. Unstained or reused pigment is rejected, making mass fake identities uneconomic.
